This skill ships no script. Every key is read by the AGENT, and an install's
own scripts may read one (a gate that reuses repo.install_command, say),
which is exactly why the values must be written down: a guessed worktrees
directory produces an orphan nobody can find, a guessed landing branch lands
finished work on the wrong line, and a guessed branch type starts the

repo._comment: The checkout this discipline governs. 'root' is the ONE main checkout that is never written to; 'worktrees_dir' is where a session working from the shared checkout creates its worktrees; an agent working from its own home creates them under that home's workspaces directory instead, which the agent skill's install context names. Both are declared locations, which is what makes an orphaned workspace findable by listing them (SKILL.md section 1.3 has the argument). 'landing_branch' is the DEFAULT branch finished work merges into - an engagement may declare a different one, and SKILL.md's evidence rules turn on never assuming this value. 'install_command' is the full per-worktree dependency install, run from the worktree root, covering EVERY root that carries its own lockfile: it is the single source for that list, so a root added to the repo is added here in the same change. 'dev_stack_command' brings up the isolated local stack; say in CONTEXT.md whether it claims a per-worktree port slot.
repo.install_command: npm ci && npm ci --prefix subpackage-a && npm ci --prefix subpackage-b

environments._comment: The environment names this install uses, in the shared role vocabulary the repo-and-environments skill defines. SKILL.md references only 'live', when it says which branch a fix for the live line cuts from; the rest are here so the branch table in CONTEXT.md can be written in the same words. The branch-to-environment map itself is NOT here: it is single-sourced by the repo-and-environments skill, and a second copy of it is a second thing to drift. 'live_copy' is a non-live environment holding a copy of live's data; omit the key where the install has none.

naming._comment: How an agent names a branch and a commit subject (SKILL.md section 1.1). 'branch' and 'subject' are forms built from the segments <agent>, <Agent>, <type>, <scope>, <slug> and <subject>; a form may leave out any of them, and one without <agent> and <Agent> is the form for a repository whose agents all commit under one identity. <slug> here is kebab-case. 'types' is the CLOSED list a <type> segment takes, each with its meaning: SKILL.md never enumerates it and nothing else in the install should either, since a second enumeration, or a written count of it, rots without looking like one. Adding or retiring a type edits this key, plus any place the install's project instructions repeat it, which CONTEXT.md names. The exempt lanes and CI subjects are not here: CONTEXT.md lists them byte-exact.
naming.subject: <Agent>: <type>(<scope>): <subject>

types.chore: maintenance that is neither a feature nor a fix, including an integration branch that merges and pushes and owns no change of its own
types.docs: documents only, including a design package or a spike that produces no product code
